title: Music Fundamentals III: Triads and Seventh Chords

guide.summary: Unit 3 covers triads and seventh chords: qualities, inversions, figured-bass symbols, and diatonic chords in major and minor keys with Roman numerals.

sections.heading: Triads
sections.body: Triads stack thirds: major (M3 + m3), minor (m3 + M3), diminished (m3 + m3), augmented (M3 + M3). Inversion depends on the bass: root position (5/3, no figure needed), first inversion (6/3, written 6, third in the bass), second inversion (6/4, fifth in the bass). In major keys, diatonic triads are I ii iii IV V vi vii°; in minor (with raised leading tone for V and vii°), i ii° III iv V VI vii°. Uppercase numerals indicate major, lowercase minor, ° diminished, + augmented.

sections.heading: Seventh chords
sections.body: Seventh chords add a seventh above the root. Qualities: major seventh (MM7: major triad + M7), dominant seventh (Mm7: major triad + m7), minor seventh (mm7), half-diminished seventh (ø7: diminished triad + m7), fully diminished seventh (°7: diminished triad + d7). Inversion figures: root position 7, first inversion 6/5, second inversion 4/3, third inversion 4/2 (or 2, seventh in the bass). In major: IM7 ii7 iii7 IVM7 V7 vi7 viiø7; in harmonic minor: V7 and vii°7.

sections.heading: Figured bass
sections.body: Figured bass shows intervals above the bass, in the key signature unless altered. An accidental alone (e.g., ♯) refers to the third above the bass; a slash or plus through a number means raise it. Realizing figured bass means choosing the upper voices that complete the indicated chord. In part writing from figured bass, first identify each chord's root and quality, then follow voice-leading rules.

keyTakeaways: Diatonic chords in major and minor.
V and vii° in minor use the raised 7.
commonMistakes: Labeling inversions by the top note rather than the bass.
Forgetting to raise 7 in minor V.
Confusing half- and fully diminished sevenths.
examTips: Find the root by stacking the notes in thirds.
Memorize the qualities of diatonic chords.

practice.prompt: Realize this figured bass in four voices (SATB) in C major. Bass: C3 (no figure) – F2 (no figure) – G2 (7) – C3 (no figure). Give the soprano, alto, and tenor pitch for each chord, label each with a Roman numeral, and avoid parallel fifths and octaves.

rubric.description: I: e.g., S E4, A C4, T G3, B C3.
IV: e.g., S F4, A C4, T A3, B F2 (root doubled).
V7: e.g., S F4 (prepared seventh), A B3, T G3, B G2 (incomplete V7, root doubled).
I: e.g., S E4, A C4, T G3, B C3 (complete).
Chordal seventh F resolves down by step to E.
No parallel fifths or octaves in any connection.
Upper voices within an octave of each other; voices in range.

practice.sampleResponse:
Roman numerals: I – IV – V7 – I.
Chord 1 (I): S E4, A C4, T G3, B C3.
Chord 2 (IV): S F4, A C4, T A3, B F2.
Chord 3 (V7): S F4, A B3, T G3, B G2. The F in the soprano is the chordal seventh, prepared by the common tone from IV; the chord omits its fifth (D) and doubles the root.
Chord 4 (I): S E4, A C4, T G3, B C3.
The seventh (F) resolves down to E, the leading tone (B) resolves up to C, and the incomplete V7 resolves to a complete I. Bass and soprano move in contrary motion from I to IV and from V7 to I, avoiding parallel fifths and octaves.
